verdictNotes: No blocking defect. The product bytes match the reduced P2CG1G2 contract (units.json/roadmap.json at the head): all five creators bind expectedCampaignId to the campaign id (which differs from the match id in every runtime row), the identity-first guest join consumes G2A exactly as CF-G2A-5 requires, the registry/seat design (G2-RESEAT-1) is sound under every reseat ordering I could construct, and no path adopts state or events from a foreign campaign. Ledger discipline holds commit by commit; RED (34/129) and GREEN (129/129) reproduce; 32/32 required checks succeed by name on the exact head; the byte-identical controls hold. The notes are six surviving mutants of mine (all test gaps or latent hardening, none a GREEN defect), one latent API hazard in the seat module, one orphaned-socket observation on a practically unreachable path, and the ML6 "equivalent" claim which I downgrade to a defence-in-depth test gap.

reviewClassEvidence.note: The unit's five sensitive review classes with the reviewer's section 3 paragraphs verbatim (the concurrency paragraph is followed by eight reseat-ordering bullets, also verbatim). No class records a defect. Each verdict field is the closure's reading, not reviewer text.

authority.finding: **Authority.** The client gains no authority. The guest join reads campaign identity from the server through the verified identity mode and still submits a CampaignJoin that the WS layer gates (seat/revocation unchanged; auth.ts, token.ts, Player.ts untouched). The entry panel validates matchId/campaignId/status before any socket and refuses 400/401/404 finally (E10 rows; no anonymous fallback; exactly one invites request). The launch page never closes a transport it did not create and sends only through a transport bound to its own seat (RV9 caught). The surface refuses a stored transport bound to another campaign on the same match (CF-H16 rows; MSu1/MSu2 and RV9 caught). Bound/unbound join bytes and the numeric legacy ACK are identical before any offer (pinned), so nothing is activated on the wire.

privacy.verdict: PASS (adds no disclosure; the PRIV-1 correlation stays the B15 hold, neither widened nor narrowed)
privacy.finding: **Privacy.** Bearer only in the Authorization header, URL exactly ?campaignIdentity=1, cache:'no-store' (E1 row; ME5 caught). No token= anywhere (asserted on every refusal row). No /api/multiplayer/matches/ read (asserted). The resolved campaignId is used for the mirror and the guest campaign; the identity response's layout/status are not stored. The only disclosure in play is G2A's recorded PRIV-1 correlation (campaignId to anyone with a live code and a self-signed bearer), which G2 neither widens nor narrows; it stays a B15 obligation (R-PRIV-1). Error strings shown to the user are the route's constant bodies.

replay.verdict: PASS with notes (post-adoption filtering of foreign legacy events rests on campaignMirrorStore and the host fold, which G2 does not own; CF-H6 pinned)
replay.finding: **Replay.** The guest adopts only the first snapshot whose event.campaignId AND payload.state.campaignId equal the identity-resolved id (MS4 and both "another campaign" rows; a mismatch rejects without touching the mirror). The transport's legacy path forwards every campaign frame regardless of campaignId (unchanged from base), so post-adoption filtering of foreign legacy events rests on campaignMirrorStore (applySnapshot/applyEvent refuse a different campaignId once set, lines 265/306) and on the host fold/consumer, which G2 does not own. Snapshot-at-revision-0 semantics are unchanged (applySnapshot(snapshot, 0)). A replacement B's listener is attached only after A's is detached, so a late A frame publishes nothing (pinned). CF-H6 is genuinely pinned: a bound host against a legacy server keeps one socket across remount at 2T, and my re-run of the consumer mutant RM-G9 fails exactly that row (1/129).

idempotency.finding: **Idempotency.** Same-object registration is a no-op without notification (MT3 caught). releaseActiveTransport is identity-guarded so a late A.close() never drops B (MT2 and the stale-timeout row). settle() in the seat wait is re-entrant safe (second call clears nothing new, stopFollowing is idempotent, resolve/reject no-ops). unsubscribe deletes a per-subscription wrapper (RV5 caught). The replacement resend is sent once per seating (ML3 caught, "exactly once" row). _resetCampaignSyncTransportsForTest clears observers (MT6 caught).

concurrency.verdict: PASS with notes (reentrant attach guard correct but unpinned, RV4; N3 superseded A left open on an unreachable path)
concurrency.finding: **Concurrency / reseat races.** I traced each ordering against the seat module:
orderings: Seat replaced between snapshot and adoption: the wait resolves on A's frame, the foreign takeover lands, the post-await boundCampaignSyncTransport(seat) check refuses (row pinned; RV12 caught: a weaker "any active transport" check adopts).
Same-seat replacement B during the wait: subscribe-then-reconcile follows to B, snapshot heard on B completes the join with no render (pinned). A is left open (note N3).
Foreign replacement during the wait: the follower detaches from A, seats nothing, the one fixed 10 s timeout rejects, A is closed, the foreign socket is neither adopted nor closed (pinned).
Unmount mid-join: the per-attempt AbortController rejects the wait, the catch closes A and returns without setState (pinned; ME4 caught).

Reentrant registry change inside an observer: observers are snapshotted and isolated (MT4/MT5 caught); reconcile re-reads the getter and is idempotent on next === seated; the attach-time reentrancy guard (seated !== next -> off()) is correct but unpinned (RV4 survived).
Server-initiated close: onclose releases the slot only if it is still the active object and notifies followers (RV6 caught by the CF12 row).
Registration order: setActiveTransport is the last statement of connectCampaignSyncTransport, after every socket handler is installed, so an observer never sees a half-built transport.

Cross-campaign binding on the same match: connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport refuses by campaignId (pre-existing G1 logic, now reachable because both surface creators pass expectedCampaignId); boundCampaignSyncTransport additionally checks playerId and role for the launch/entry seats. The stored connect itself still checks only campaignId, not role/playerId (pre-existing; note N5).

items.finding: waitForSeatCampaignSnapshot registers the abort listener but never checks signal.aborted; a caller passing an already-aborted signal waits for the full timeout or, worse, a snapshot. The entry panel is safe only because of the synchronous throwIfAborted at CampaignCoopEntryPanel.tsx:315 (RV7 shows removing that line survives the suite: no row unmounts during identity resolution). One-line hardening: if (signal.aborted) { reject; return; } before subscribing.

The role check in boundCampaignSyncTransport is unpinned (RV1 survived; the author's MS1 pins playerId only). Unreachable today (one player, one role per match in a tab) but part of the registered seat contract.

On a successful join heard through a same-seat replacement B, the superseded A is neither closed nor owned: open socket, running heartbeat, and (legacy) duplicate numeric ACKs from a second socket for the same player. Unreachable today (no second same-seat creator exists before the guest campaign is created); pre-existing registry semantics (base also overwrote without closing).

The replacement resend reads localChoiceRef.current, but the "exactly once" row never changes the choice first, so RV10 (resend the default) survives. Add a row: pick command-hq, then reseat, expect command-hq.

connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport refuses a stored transport only by campaignId; role/playerId mismatches on the same match are returned to the surface as-is. The seat module covers launch/entry; the surface's own binding relies on the consumer's campaignId check. Pre-existing (G1), not a G2 regression.

Listener lifetime after dispose is unpinned: RV11 (cleanup skips stopFollowing) and RV3 (settle keeps following) survive. Observable as a late post-unmount frame publishing participation (RV11) or listener accumulation per join (RV3).

With CF-H16 delivered, a foreign-bound transport on the same match leaves the surface with no transport and no recovery until that transport closes (the slot stays occupied). Correct refusal; the UX/recovery of that state belongs to the consumer's next owner.

ML6 is not strictly equivalent: with the matchId check removed, a frame carrying a foreign matchId would be published under that foreign key (publishCoopParticipation uses message.matchId), observable by a subscriber on that key. Defence in depth, unpinnable from this page alone; Low. ME6 is equivalent under current wiring (abort only fires on unmount; the suppressed setState has no observer).
